sentences.text: A cross-sectional study examined 36 pairs of individuals with Huntington's disease and their close family members, finding that patients reported lower quality of life, reduced emotional awareness, and higher social anxiety compared to their relatives.

The analysis revealed that a patient's quality of life was most strongly linked to their level of social anxiety, while the ability to regulate attention to internal bodily signals was specifically associated with daily functioning, and caregiver stress was predicted by patient apathy and difficulties with listening to bodily signals.

The authors suggest that dysfunction in sensing internal body signals contributes to emotional problems and caregiver burden in Huntington's disease, noting that while social anxiety directly lowers quality of life, interoceptive issues may also indirectly affect it through other symptoms like apathy.
